title: Fast and slow
summary: Hear the same tune at different speeds and tap the pulse as it changes.

hook.text: Sing *Happy Birthday* in your head like a sleepy lullaby. Now sing it as fast as you can. Same tune, same sounds. So what changed? Press one key below slowly, then quickly, to feel the difference.

explore.text: Choose one key. Tap it in a steady [[pulse|pulse]], nice and slow, like a sleepy heartbeat. Now squeeze the ticks closer together, keeping them even. Then slow down again.
explore.goal: Tap one key slowly, then quickly, then slowly again.

cards.text: The speed of the pulse is the [[tempo|tempo]]. In a slow tempo the ticks are far apart. In a fast tempo they are close together. The tune stays the same; only the gaps between the ticks change.
You can count a tempo: how many ticks fit into one minute. 60 ticks a minute is one tick every second. 120 ticks a minute is two every second, so it is twice as fast.
Whatever the tempo, the pulse stays steady. In the tapping questions you hear a count-in first. Those clicks tell you the tempo, so listen to them and match the gap between them.

alternative.text: Think of walking, jogging and sprinting. Your feet land evenly every time, but a faster pace puts the steps closer together. A slow walk is a slow tempo and a sprint is a fast one. Same legs, same steadiness, different gaps.

questions.prompt: The same tune is played twice. Which clip is faster?
questions.hint: Tap along with each clip. In which one do your taps come closer together?

options.reason: Clip B ticks slowly, with the ticks far apart. Clip A plays the same tune with the ticks closer together, so it is the faster one.

questions.prompt: Listen to the slow clicks, then tap once on every click.
questions.hint: Do not rush. Wait for the count-in to show you how far apart the clicks are, then match it.

questions.prompt: A tune speeds up. What changes?
questions.hint: Think about your foot tapping to a tune that gets faster. What happens to the gap between taps?

options.reason: Loudness is a different thing. When a tune speeds up, the ticks come closer together.
A faster pulse can be perfectly steady. The ticks are just closer together, and each gap is still the same.

questions.prompt: Put these in order, from the slowest [[tempo|tempo]] to the fastest.
questions.hint: More ticks in one minute means faster music. Which one has the fewest?

payload.reason: More ticks in a minute means a faster tempo, so the order is 40, then 90, then 150.

questions.prompt: Listen to the quick clicks, then tap once on every click.
questions.hint: The taps come quickly, but it is still one tap per click. Keep your hand loose and ride the count-in.

questions.prompt: Listen, then tap on every click.
questions.hint: Let the count-in show you the speed, then match it.

questions.prompt: The same tune is played twice. Which clip is slower?
questions.hint: Tap along with each clip. In which one do your taps come further apart?

options.reason: Clip B has its ticks close together, so it is the faster one. Clip A plays the same tune with the ticks further apart, which makes it slower.

questions.hint: Compare how many ticks fit into one minute.

options.reason: That is only one tick every second. 100 ticks in a minute come quicker, so that is the faster tempo.

questions.prompt: Listen, then tap on every click.
questions.hint: Keep the taps even. Land on each click, not between them.

questions.prompt: Match each [[tempo|tempo]] to how often the ticks come.
questions.hint: There are 60 seconds in a minute. 60 ticks a minute is one tick every second.

left.reason: 60 ticks in 60 seconds is one tick every second.
120 ticks in 60 seconds is two ticks every second.
30 ticks in 60 seconds is one tick every 2 seconds.

questions.prompt: The same tune is played three times. Which clip is the slowest?
questions.hint: Tap along with each clip and find the one where your taps are furthest apart.

options.reason: Clip A is quicker than clip C. Its ticks are closer together, so it is not the slowest.
Clip B has the ticks closest together, so it is the fastest. The slowest is clip C.

questions.prompt: The [[tempo|tempo]] goes from 60 ticks a minute to 120. How does the music feel?
questions.hint: Twice as many ticks fit into the same minute.

options.reason: More ticks in a minute means the ticks are closer together, which is faster, not slower.
The number of ticks in a minute has doubled, so the ticks are closer together. The music is faster.

questions.hint: Match the count-in, then keep the same gap between taps.

points: The speed of the pulse is the [[tempo|tempo]]. In a slow tempo the ticks are far apart; in a fast tempo they are close together.
You can count tempo as ticks in one minute: 60 ticks a minute is one every second, and 120 is twice as fast.
At any tempo the pulse stays steady. Listen to the count-in first and match its gap.
